---
title: "Did Remote Work Revive Small French Municipalities? Population and Housing Market Dynamics after the Pandemic"
author: "Burcu Bölgen & Laura Moldovanu"
format: html
editor: visual
---

## Introduction

This project asks whether small French municipalities that were better suited to remote work before the pandemic experienced stronger residential inflows, faster housing price growth and more business creation after COVID-19 than otherwise comparable municipalities.

The pandemic led to a rapid and lasting expansion of remote work, which may have altered the relative attractiveness of large cities compared with small towns and rural areas. Population growth in these areas, however, does not by itself indicate that remote work was the driving factor. Our approach is to compare municipalities according to their suitability for remote work before 2020, which we measure through the occupational structure of their residents and their access to fibre broadband. If remote work played a role, the post-pandemic changes should be more pronounced in municipalities that combined a large share of teleworkable occupations with good connectivity.

## Data cleaning

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

### Municipality codes

```{r}
cog <- read_csv("data/cog_table_passage_2026.csv", col_types = cols(.default = "c")) |>
  filter(NIVGEO == "COM")

cog_map <- cog |>
  select(starts_with("CODGEO_")) |>
  pivot_longer(-CODGEO_2026, names_to = "year", values_to = "old_code",
               names_prefix = "CODGEO_") |>
  bind_rows(cog |> transmute(CODGEO_2026, year = "2026", old_code = CODGEO_2026)) |>
  filter(!is.na(old_code)) |>
  arrange(desc(year)) |>
  distinct(old_code, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(old_code, code_2026 = CODGEO_2026)

nrow(cog_map)
n_distinct(cog_map$code_2026)
```

### Census 2017

```{r}
rp2017 <- read_csv("data/rp2017_emploi_commune.csv", col_types = cols(.default = "c")) |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("C17"), as.numeric))

telework_2017 <- rp2017 |>
  inner_join(cog_map, by = c("CODGEO" = "old_code")) |>
  group_by(code_2026) |>
  summarise(employed_2017 = sum(C17_ACTOCC1564),
            managers_interm_2017 = sum(C17_ACTOCC1564_CS3 + C17_ACTOCC1564_CS4)) |>
  mutate(telework_index = if_else(employed_2017 > 0,
                                  managers_interm_2017 / employed_2017, NA_real_))

rp2017 |> anti_join(cog_map, by = c("CODGEO" = "old_code")) |> nrow()
summary(telework_2017$telework_index)
```

### ARCEP fibre

```{r}
fibre <- read_csv("data/arcep_fibre_communes.csv", col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

fibre_2019 <- fibre |>
  transmute(code = `Code commune`,
            premises_2026 = as.numeric(`Meilleure estimation des locaux T2 2026`),
            fibre_premises_2019 = as.numeric(`T4 2019`)) |>
  inner_join(cog_map, by = c("code" = "old_code")) |>
  group_by(code_2026) |>
  summarise(premises_2026 = sum(premises_2026),
            fibre_premises_2019 = sum(fibre_premises_2019)) |>
  mutate(fibre_share_2019 = if_else(premises_2026 > 0,
                                    pmin(fibre_premises_2019 / premises_2026, 1), NA_real_))

fibre |> anti_join(cog_map, by = c("Code commune" = "old_code")) |> nrow()
summary(fibre_2019$fibre_share_2019)
```

### SIRENE

```{r}
sirene <- read_csv("data/sirene_creations_by_municipality_year.csv",
                   col_types = cols(codeCommuneEtablissement = "c",
                                    year = "i", n_creations = "i"))

arm_map <- tibble(
  old_code = c(sprintf("751%02d", 1:20), sprintf("6938%d", 1:9), sprintf("132%02d", 1:16)),
  code_2026 = c(rep("75056", 20), rep("69123", 9), rep("13055", 16))
)
sirene_map <- bind_rows(cog_map, arm_map)

sirene_clean <- sirene |>
  filter(year <= 2025) |>
  inner_join(sirene_map, by = c("codeCommuneEtablissement" = "old_code")) |>
  group_by(code_2026, year) |>
  summarise(n_creations = sum(n_creations), .groups = "drop")

sirene |>
  anti_join(sirene_map, by = c("codeCommuneEtablissement" = "old_code")) |>
  summarise(unmatched_codes = n_distinct(codeCommuneEtablissement),
            creations_lost = sum(n_creations))

sirene |>
  anti_join(sirene_map, by = c("codeCommuneEtablissement" = "old_code")) |>
  group_by(codeCommuneEtablissement) |>
  summarise(creations = sum(n_creations)) |>
  arrange(desc(creations)) |>
  head(10)
```

### Summary of the cleaning and matching

All sources are linked through the INSEE municipality code. Because French municipalities frequently merge, a code that existed in one year may no longer exist in another. Using the COG correspondence table, we built a list linking every municipality code that existed since 2003 (36716 codes) to its code in 2026 geography (34876 municipalities). Each source was then converted to 2026 codes and the values of merged municipalities were added together.

For the 2017 census data, 45 codes could not be matched. These were the districts of Paris, Lyon and Marseille, which were listed separately even though the data also included the three cities as a whole. We therefore removed them. The remote-work index could not be calculated for 102 municipalities because they had no declared employed residents.

For ARCEP fiber data, only 4 codes could not be matched. AT the end of 2019, more than half of the municipalities had no premises connected to fiber. This means that the fiber shared is often zero. For this reason, we could also use a simple indicator showing whether fiber was available or not.

In the SIRENE data , establishments in Paris, Lyon and Marseille were identified by district. We assigned these districts to their respective cities to make the data consistent with the other sources. The other unmatched codes, representing around 27986new establishments, belong to overseas territories that are not included in the COG municipality list. These territories were excluded from the study. 
Finally, we removed 2026, because the data for this year is incomplete.

## Main variables

- `code_2026`: the INSEE code of municipality in 2026. This code is used to connect all the date from different sources.
- `employed_2017`: the number of people aged 15 to 64 who had a job in the municipality in 2017.
- `managers_interm_2017`: the number of employed people who were managers or had intermediate-level jobs in 2017. These types of jobs are more likely to allow remote work.
- `telework_index`: the percentage of employed people who were managers or had intermediate-level jobs in 2017. It shows how suitable the municipality was for remote work before the pandemic.
- `premises_2026`: the estimated total number of premises (homes and business buildings) in the municipality, according to ARCEP.
- `fibre_premises_2019`: the number of premises that had access to fiber broadband at the end of 2019.
- `fibre_share_2019`: the percentage of premises that could access fiber broadband in 2019. It shows how easy it was to work remotely from that municipality before the pandemic.
- `year`: the year when whe establishments were created, between 2014 and 2025.
- `n_creations`: the number of the new establishments created in the municipality each ear, based on data from the SIRENE register.
